question: Name the scientist who discovered X-rays in 1895.
explanation: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895, changing the face of modern medical diagnostics forever. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary medical benefit of using X-rays in clinical practice?

options.A: Viewing internal body structures without surgery
options.B: Measuring the exact electrical activity of the heart
options.C: Destroying harmful bacteria on the skin surface
options.D: Treating chronic high blood pressure conditions

explanation: X-rays allow healthcare providers to look inside the human body non-invasively to check bones and organs. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h1)

question: Which metal is commonly used as the target in an X-ray tube anode?
explanation: Tungsten is chosen because it has a very high melting point and can withstand the intense heat generated by bombarding electrons. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h2)

question: Where do X-rays fall on the electromagnetic spectrum relative to visible light?
explanation: X-rays have much shorter wavelengths and higher frequencies than visible light, giving them greater penetrating power. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h2)

question: What term describes tissues that allow X-ray beams to pass through them easily?
explanation: Radiolucent structures, like lungs filled with air, offer little resistance to X-rays and show up dark on radiographs. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why do bones appear white on a standard X-ray image?

options.A: They stain the X-ray film a milky white color
options.B: They emit their own bright light when exposed
options.C: They absorb or block most of the X-ray photons
options.D: They let all the radiation pass straight through

explanation: Dense bone tissue blocks the X-rays from hitting the film or digital plate behind it, creating a white shadow. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h3)

question: Which of the five basic radiographic densities appears the darkest on an X-ray film?
explanation: Air offers zero resistance to the beam, so maximum X-rays reach the film to produce a black appearance. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h4)

question: A patient swallows a metallic coin. How will this object most likely appear on an X-ray?
explanation: Metal is extremely dense and blocks almost all X-ray photons, showing up as a very bright white shape on the image. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h4)

question: What does the acronym ALARA stand for in radiation safety?
explanation: ALARA is the golden rule of radiation protection, ensuring patients receive only the minimum necessary dose. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h5)

question: Why is special caution required when considering X-rays for a pregnant woman?

options.A: Pregnancy turns all soft tissues completely radiopaque
options.B: Radiation causes the ultrasound equipment to malfunction
options.C: Developing fetal cells are sensitive to ionizing radiation
options.D: X-ray machines do not work properly on pregnant bodies

explanation: Rapidly dividing cells in a developing fetus are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of ionizing radiation. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common reason to perform a chest X-ray in clinical practice?
explanation: Chest X-rays evaluate the heart and lungs, not uterine contractions, which are monitored via palpation or electronic fetal monitoring. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h6)

question: Why do plain X-rays remain widely used in resource-limited healthcare settings across Nigeria?

options.A: They are relatively fast, affordable, and accessible
options.B: They are completely harmless to a developing fetus
options.C: They provide clearer 3D color images than MRIs
options.D: They do not use any form of ionizing radiation

explanation: Plain radiographs offer a reliable, cost-effective diagnostic option where advanced imaging machines are scarce. [learn more](BMP112_U6_T4#BMP112_U6_T4_h6)
